reasons: The numerator selector for redis.keyspace.hits uses otel_metric_type="gauge", but the dataset only has this metric as sum (dataset_types: [sum]), so the numerator matches no series. The denominator uses sum for the same metric, so the two sides are inconsistent.

A gauge selector wrapped in rate() would also violate the rule that rate() is only for monotonic sums. The numerator should use otel_metric_type="sum", matching the definition (monotonic sum) and the dataset.

The Datadog $host template variable has prefix host and default *, so it should produce a host=~"$host" matcher on both sides. The candidate omits it, so the series set differs from the request. The dataset does not list a host label among observed labels, so the label name needs confirming before the matcher is added.
$scope has no prefix and default *, so dropping it is correct. $key is not referenced by any query, so it needs no matcher.
The *100 scale and the ratio hits/(hits+misses) match the Datadog formula, and translating to a translated outcome is correct since the metrics exist as monotonic sums.
